title: Zheng Qinwen stuns Madison Keys in U.S. Open comeback from the edge of defeat
content:
NEW YORK — Trailing 5-0 in the third set, the 2024 Olympic champion Zheng Qinwen kept her comeback run at this U.S. Open alive, working her way back from match-point down to upset the No. 22 seed Madison Keys, 1-6, 7-6(3), 7-5.

Zheng, who came through the qualifying tournament, ended up splayed on the blue of the court for the third time in just under a fortnight after her dramatic comeback. The 23-year-old is rebuilding her ranking after being sidelined on and off for more than a year, following elbow surgery in July of 2025.

She was sick during qualifying and said Thursday she still isn’t feeling fully healthy — but she is rediscovering her fighting spirit.

“I always believe, especially when I was down 4-5, it was a very tough game and in that moment, I showed no emotion because I know it’s never the end until the end,” Zheng said.

“Brave is the word today… I’m just super happy to have won this match. It’s like, wow. What can I say? Wow.”

From 5-0 down in the third set, Zheng won seven games in a row to claim a win that had looked impossible. Despite such a commanding lead, Keys only earned one match point, as she served at 5-1. After catching her ball toss before serving, an attempted backhand redirect down the line, the type of shot Keys laces for a winner when she is feeling her tennis, crashed into the net.

From there, Zheng used her lofted forehand and backhand to pin Keys back, taking her toes off the baseline and asking her to either build points over the course of several shots, or take arcing balls on the rise, a decision heavy with risk.

By the 11th game of the third set, Keys was hitting herself in the head with her racket and taking her cap off in disbelief, as another groundstroke long gave Zheng the chance to serve for her sixth consecutive win at the Billie Jean King National Tennis Center.

Keys ended with 23 unforced errors on her forehand side, her stronger wing, to 18 winners. Zheng played more conservatively and chipped away at the former Australian Open champion, the crowd — which was split on Grandstand despite that Keys is American — cheering her on.

“I was just telling myself keep holding every single point, never give up,” Zheng said. “Somehow, little by little, it just happened. Finally, one time, luck is on my side.”

She will face either 2022 champion Iga Świątek or Marie Bouzková of the Czech Republic in the fourth round.
